unit_result_entry.why_material: The period integral and binomial expansion turn the critical values of a modular-form L-function into the coefficients of one polynomial. This is the foundational compression that lets a statement about a list of L-values become a statement about polynomial zero geometry.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The L-function functional equation becomes reciprocal symmetry of polynomial roots
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Applying the functional equation coefficientwise yields a self-inversive relation: every root is paired with its reciprocal transform. This identifies the symmetry circle and motivates the polynomial ‘Riemann hypothesis’ that all roots lie on it.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Encoding critical L-values in a period polynomial transports the L-function functional equation into reciprocal root symmetry; factoring that symmetry through a half-polynomial then turns the desired circle-zero statement into a count of sine or cosine sign changes.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This mechanism establishes the paper’s polynomial analogue only; it supplies no implication for the zero locations of the Riemann zeta function or the underlying modular L-function.

3. The weight 4 case
If f is a form of weight k = 4 (so m = (k −2)/2 = 1), then Pf (z) = Λ(f, 2)+Λ(f, 3)z. If ǫ(f ) = −1,
then the roots of√Pf (z) − Pf (1/z) = Λ(f, 3)(z − 1/z) are at z = ±1 and so the period polynomial
has roots at ±i/ N .
   If ǫ(f ) = 1, then with z = eiθ we have Pf (z) + Pf (1/z) = 2Λ(f, 2) + 2Λ(f, 3) cos θ. Since
Λ(f, 2) < Λ(f, 3) by Lemma 2.1, the above equation has two solutions for θ ∈ [0, 2π): namely, θ
satisfying cos θ = −Λ(f, 2)/Λ(f, 3). This completes the proof of Theorem 1.1 for weight 4.

unit_result_entry.title: Finite residual cases are closed by L-value evaluation and direct sign-change tests
unit_result_entry.why_material: The authors identify exactly which weights and levels escape the analytic criteria, enumerate newforms in Sage, compute critical L-values at high precision, test the monotone-coefficient inequality when possible, and otherwise verify the needed number of trigonometric sign changes directly. This records the logical role of computation in completing the theorem.

More importantly, the source does not preserve Sage version, commands, precision targets, rounding/error certification, exhaustive case list, or machine-readable outputs, so reproducibility and rigor of the finite closure cannot be established from this text alone.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Phase perturbation upgrades circle membership to quantitative root locations
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The same exponential approximation yields an explicit leading phase whose regularly spaced zero locations persist under a uniform small error. Evaluating on either side of each predicted phase zero traps one true root, producing the asymptotic location and equidistribution result for both functional-equation signs.
